target.title: Add universal quota planning estimates
target.body:
## Summary

- add a provider-neutral estimator that learns how many full short-window sessions the remaining long-window quota can fund
- add transient fetch freshness plus descriptor-driven pair resolution for Codex, Claude, and Antigravity
- isolate in-memory calibration by provider, account, strategy, pair, and reset window, with monotonic expiry and fail-closed lifecycle handling
- show one concise localized line on the matching long-window row: `Available full sessions: ≈N`
- keep deterministic schedule capacity and reachability typed inside Core, but do not surface them in the UI following the latest product direction in #2261

## Status

Draft implementation following the architecture in #2268 and the later UI direction in #2261.

- [x] Core estimator and focused tests
- [x] provider capability, freshness, and pair resolvers
- [x] UsageStore scope, lifecycle, TTL, and expiry
- [x] localized menu presentation across all catalogs
- [x] `make check`
- [ ] clean full `make test` run (blocked by an unrelated local Claude credential/keychain ownership suite; details below)
- [ ] redacted live-provider/menu proof

## Validation

Passed:

- `swift test --filter QuotaPlanningTests`
- `swift test --filter QuotaPlanningProviderResolutionTests`
- `swift test --filter AntigravityQuotaSummaryTests`
- `swift test --filter CodexConsumerProjectionTests`
- `swift test --filter "QuotaPlanningLifecycleTests|QuotaPlanningProviderResolutionTests|QuotaPlanningTests|CodexResetCreditOutcomeTests"` — 42 tests
- `swift test --filter "QuotaPlanningMenuPresentationTests|MenuCardOverrideIsolationTests|MenuCardHeightFingerprintTests|QuotaPlanningLifecycleTests"` — 26 tests
- `make check` — 0 SwiftFormat changes, 0 SwiftLint violations, all 22 non-English catalogs match 1,221 English keys

`make test` discovered 702 selections in 59 groups. The first 10 groups passed. Group 11 failed twice only in the pre-existing `ClaudeOAuthCredentialsStoreCLIStorageOwnershipTests` suite with eight local credential/keychain ownership errors (`.notFound`, `.decodeFailed`, and local credentials-file precedence); the sharded runner then stopped. No quota-planning test failed.

Real provider and account-sensitive menu proof was not run because repository policy requires an explicit request before live provider, cookie, or Keychain-backed probes.

Refs #2261
Design: #2268

target.title: Doubao: query Coding/Agent Plan usage via arkcli CLI
target.body:
## Summary

- Replace the Volcengine AK/SK signed API with `arkcli usage plan` CLI (SSO-based) for fetching Coding Plan and Agent Plan usage
- Split Doubao menu card into "Coding Plan" and "Agent Plan" sections with group headers
- Replace placeholder smiley icon with official Volcengine logo SVG

## Why

The signed Volcengine API (`GetCodingPlanUsage` / `GetAgentPlanUsage`) required users to obtain AK/SK credentials separately and did not work well. The `arkcli` CLI uses the same SSO session the user already has, making setup trivial - just install arkcli and `arkcli auth login`.

## Changes

- `DoubaoUsageFetcher`: new `fetchCodingPlanUsage(runArkcli:)` runs `arkcli usage plan` and decodes the JSON response. Old Volcengine signer code removed.
- `DoubaoAPIFetchStrategy`: try arkcli CLI first, fall back to Ark API key rate-limit probe.
- `MenuCardView`: split Doubao metrics into two groups (Coding Plan / Agent Plan) with section headers. Other providers unaffected (`guard provider == .doubao`).
- `ProviderIcon-doubao.svg`: official Volcengine logo (MIT-licensed, from thesvg.org).
- Tests updated to match new arkcli JSON format and strategy interface.

Closes #1724.

target.title: Add configurable descriptive agent session labels
target.body:
## Summary

- add an Agent sessions label setting with Project, Descriptive, and Descriptive + project modes
- use Codex thread titles for main sessions, named task paths for subagents, and a clear Approval review label for guardians
- keep Project as the compatibility default and fall back to the project whenever descriptive metadata is unavailable
- carry the optional descriptive name through remote session JSON without breaking older payloads

## Why

Agent session rows currently use only the working-directory basename. When several Codex sessions share one repository, every row can have the same label even though Codex already stores useful chat titles and subagent task names.

This makes the behavior configurable instead of replacing the existing label style for everyone.

## Implementation notes

- reads only the requested Codex thread rows from the newest `state_*.sqlite` database
- gracefully falls back when the database or newer columns are unavailable
- removes command preambles and caps long automatic titles at 64 characters
- continues using project names for Claude Code because equivalent title metadata is not currently exposed

## Validation

- `swift build --target CodexBarCore` passed with the compatible installed SDK
- `swift build --target CodexBarCLI` passed from current head `2370d11d57b7cfa2d95e4d95cd59c08c0af57689`
- `CodexBarCLI sessions --json` passed against live local session metadata and produced compact descriptive names
- SwiftFormat lint passed for all Sources and Tests
- app locale, documentation, packaging, signing-path, sharding, CI-path, repository-size, shell, and site checks passed
- full Swift tests and SwiftLint could not run locally because this Mac's Command Line Tools compiler, SDK, Testing framework, and SourceKit installation are mismatched; macOS CI is required before review completion

### Redacted runtime proof

Captured from current head on July 17, 2026. The first scan used the live Codex home and resolved the thread title:

```json
[
  {
    "provider": "codex",
    "source": "ide",
    "state": "active",
    "projectName": "<redacted project>",
    "sessionName": "Fix Claude reauthorization"
  }
]
```

For the missing-metadata case, the same live rollout was copied into an isolated `CODEX_HOME` with no `state_*.sqlite` database. The CLI kept the project name and returned no descriptive name:

```json
[
  {
    "provider": "codex",
    "source": "ide",
    "state": "active",
    "projectName": "<redacted project>",
    "sessionName": null
  }
]
```

That second result exercises the menu fallback: Descriptive and Descriptive + project use `projectName` when `sessionName` is absent. Project remains the persisted default.

target.title: Migrate ClaudeOAuthRefreshFailureGate fingerprint override to a task-local scope
target.body:
## Summary
Migrate `ClaudeOAuthRefreshFailureGate`'s fingerprint-provider test override off the unsynchronized
process-global `nonisolated(unsafe) static var fingerprintProviderOverride` onto a task-local scope,
mirroring `KeychainAccessPreflight`. Part of #2204.

## Changes
- Replace the static + its `setFingerprintProviderOverrideForTesting` setter with a
  `FingerprintProviderOverrideStore` (`@unchecked Sendable`), a `@TaskLocal` store, and sync + async
  `withFingerprintProviderOverrideForTesting` scopes. `currentFingerprint()` now reads the task-local store.
- The non-macOS stub gains the matching `with…` scopes (loose `(() -> Any?)?` — `AuthFingerprint` is
  macOS-only, as with the prior setter stub).
- Move the ~10 test call sites from `set…{ }` / `defer set…(nil)` to the scoped
  `with…{ provider } operation: { … }` form (unblocks-on-fingerprint-change semantics preserved — the
  provider closure captures the mutated `var` by reference).

## Validation
- `make check` → 0 violations / 1465 files.
- Full suite, contract config (`GROUP_SIZE=4 TIMEOUT=120 RETRY=0`): 660 selections / 165 groups, all
  pass (one keychain-live-proof group timed out under local concurrent-build load and recovered;
  re-run isolated = 4 suites pass in 0.79s — unrelated to this diff). Migrated
  `ClaudeOAuthRefreshFailureGateTests` pass clean in 0.038s.
- Behavior-neutral: overrides were never written outside `…ForTesting` seams; task-local scoping
  eliminates the unsynchronized global rather than locking it.

## Related
- Part of https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2204 · follows #2239, #2240.

## Out of scope
- Remaining #2204 seams (`CookieHeaderCache`, `KeychainAccessGate`) — separate PRs. No account/auth-file
  behavior changes. Screenshots not applicable (non-UI).

## Notes
- No CHANGELOG entry — internal test synchronization only.


## Real-behavior proof

Fresh build from this PR head (`bd23e63`), then the migrated `ClaudeOAuthRefreshFailureGateTests` suite run under **ThreadSanitizer** — the `@TaskLocal` `FingerprintProviderOverrideStore` is per-task-isolated by construction, so this confirms no data race remains on the override path the old `nonisolated(unsafe) static var` raced on. Swift 6.3.3, arm64 macOS.

**Zero remaining callers of the removed setter** (repo-wide); the task-local scope is the sole override path:

```
$ grep -rn "setFingerprintProviderOverrideForTesting" Sources Tests
(no matches — 0 call sites)
$ grep -rc "withFingerprintProviderOverrideForTesting" Tests   # scoped call sites
10
```

**ThreadSanitizer — full migrated suite:**

```
$ swift test --sanitize=thread --filter "ClaudeOAuthRefreshFailureGateTests"
Build complete! (94.69s)
✔ Suite ClaudeOAuthRefreshFailureGateTests passed after 0.023 seconds.
✔ Test run with 11 tests in 1 suite passed after 0.024 seconds.
```

ThreadSanitizer reported **0 data races**. The migration removes the unsynchronized process-global rather than locking it, so parallel test execution can no longer interleave a write and read on shared override state.

Authored with Claude.
